statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is low at 14% while Stress is extreme at 83%.
recommendation: Tail remains below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. NQ trades at 29,340.75, down 0.37%, and has extended the session low to 29,326.75 in the last hour, holding within about 15 points of it. Holding near a freshly made extreme is the one tail amplifier present, and it lifts Tail three points to 14%. It is not corroborated elsewhere: the decline is a slow 0.62% drift over more than ten hours, VIX is only 16.67, and S&P 500 and Dow futures are higher on the same session, so the weakness reads as rotation out of long-duration technology rather than aggregate risk reduction. Stress stays extreme on Brent at $102.06, a 4.87% 10-year at its highest since October 2023, and roughly 60% priced odds of a September rate increase. A narrow danger window is published from 12:10 to 14:00 UTC, covering the 12:15 UTC ECB decision, the 12:30 UTC producer price and jobless claims releases and the 13:30 UTC US cash open, where the published conditional Tail reaches the watch band.
headline: NQ 29,340.75 extends the session low to 29,326.75 and holds near it while ES and YM stay higher, with VIX 16.67, Brent $102.06 and a 4.87% 10-year keeping Stress extreme into the 12:15 UTC ECB decision and 12:30 UTC producer price release
body:
Observed evidence at the assessment cutoff: Nasdaq-100 E-mini futures trade at 29,340.75, down 108.00 points or 0.37% against a 29,448.75 prior settle, inside a session range of 29,326.75 to 29,508.25 after opening near 29,458.50. The contract opened close to the session high, retreated through the European morning and has, in the last hour, extended the low from 29,359.25 to 29,326.75. Price now sits roughly 15 points above that low, so the market is holding near a session extreme rather than retracing from it. That is the one genuine tail amplifier present. Against it, the move is slow and shallow in amplitude: the full 181-point range is about 0.62% and the decline has taken more than ten hours, which is drift rather than the persistent directional efficiency that overwhelms mean reversion.

The weakness is also Nasdaq-specific rather than a broad risk-off impulse. S&P 500 futures are +0.02% and Dow futures +0.19% on the same session, while Nasdaq futures are -0.36%, so the index is underperforming on rotation out of long-duration technology rather than on an aggregate flight from equity risk. Volatility confirms the same reading: VIX is 16.67, up modestly on the day within a 16.29 to 16.67 range and still near the lower half of the summer distribution. Delayed latest-session context shows all seven tracked semiconductors lower, with a mean change of -0.78%, and five of eight megacaps lower, which is consistent with rotation pressure concentrated in the rate-sensitive complex.

Cross-asset conditions remain restrictive and are the reason Stress stays extreme. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.87%, up about three basis points and at its highest since October 2023, with the 2-year at 4.45%. Brent trades at $102.06, up 0.79%, and WTI near $97.3, up about 1.5%. The driver is the continuing exchange of strikes around the Strait of Hormuz: Iran attacked ten ships near the strait on Wednesday after the United States sank five Iranian tankers, very large crude carrier rates to China have reached almost $800,000 a day, and Saudi Arabia has begun rerouting barrels north through the Red Sea. Reported market pricing places roughly a 60% probability on a Federal Reserve rate increase at the 15-16 September meeting.

The near-term catalyst structure is dense. The ECB publishes its decision at 12:15 UTC, with President Lagarde's press conference following, and a rate increase is widely expected; US producer prices, core producer prices and weekly jobless claims all land at 12:30 UTC; existing home sales follow at 14:00 UTC; and the US cash open is at 13:30 UTC. Two independent repricings therefore overlap inside a single clock hour, with the cash open immediately behind them. That stack is why the published conditional path lifts Tail into the watch band for the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC hours and why a narrow danger window is published from 12:10 to 14:00 UTC. Consistent with the standing method, a scheduled catalyst is treated as a checkpoint rather than as already-observed structure: hypothetical post-release alignment is not counted before the data prints, and the conditional path decays once orderly two-way price discovery is re-established.

Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green) for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, with Tail at 14%, eleven points below the 25% block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping. Supplementary Finviz cross-asset context was available but flagged partial, with its economic-calendar section unavailable, so it was used only as delayed confirming context alongside the primary-source research above.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 10:00 UTC the mapped policy state was EA_ON in 23 of the 24 slots, with a single WATCH hour at 12:00 UTC on 9 September when Tail reached 20% during a trend-down European session. Tail ranged from 8% to 20% and held a narrow 8-11% band for the last nineteen hours as retracements kept appearing at both ends of the range. Stress stayed in the extreme band throughout, between 80% and 83%, as Brent held above $100 and the 10-year set successive cycle highs. Confidence held between 87% and 89%. Every slot in the window has a published Claude assessment, so no hour is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The published conditional path holds Tail at 14% in the current hour, lifts it to 21% for the 12:00 UTC hour where the ECB decision and the US producer price release overlap, and to a horizon peak of 23% in the 13:00 UTC hour where any delayed second leg would meet the US cash open. It then decays across the US afternoon from 19% to 13%, with a 15% power-hour step, and to a 9-11% band overnight before rebuilding to 13-14% into the European session that precedes Friday's consumer price release. Only the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots map to WATCH, and no slot reaches the 25% block threshold on current evidence. Stress stays in the extreme band for almost the whole horizon because the oil and yield backdrop is unlikely to change materially within it. Confidence declines with distance, from 87% now to 59% at the far end, which is the normal decay of evidence quality rather than a deterioration in the current reading.
